name: Mādhava Ghoṣa
add: Nandgram Dham: of a kāyastha family of northern Rāḍha; traditionally called «the singer of Vṛndāvana». His later śrīpāṭa: Dāiṅhāṭ near Kāṭoyā.

name: Śrī Mādhava Tīrtha
add: Nandgram Dham: born Viṣṇu Śāstrī, c. 1214 (Śaka 1136, Śrīla Prabhupāda's purport to Madhya 9.245); the third pontiff after Madhva. His guru was Narahari Tīrtha, the pontiff before him; he ordained and installed Akṣobhya Tīrtha as his successor. He founded the Majjigenahalli (Tambehalli) Maṭha near Mulbagal. His remains are said to have been laid first at Hampi and later moved to Mannur.

name: Śrī Mādhavendra Purī
add: Nandgram Dham: also Mādhava Purī; a sannyāsī of the Madhva (Tattvavādī) order under Lakṣmīpati Tīrtha; his dates are not fixed (Wikipedia estimates c. 1420–1490). Chief disciples: Īśvara Purī and Advaita Ācārya. His samādhi is at Remuṇā, beside the Kṣīra-corā Gopīnātha temple.

name: Śrī Mādhavī Devī
add: Nandgram Dham: «an elderly lady who always performed austerities… very advanced in devotional service» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya 2.104).

name: Śrī Madhu Paṇḍita
add: Nandgram Dham: Saibonā is about two miles from Khaḍadaha; he had set up the worship of Rādhā-Nandadulāl there before coming to Vṛndāvana by Gadādhara Paṇḍita's order (some accounts: trained in Vṛndāvana by Paramānanda Bhaṭṭācārya). He served Gopīnātha at Vaṁśīvaṭa for several decades; his samādhi is in the Rādhā-Gopīnātha temple compound, near its eastern gate.

name: Vidyāvācaspati
add: Nandgram Dham: son of Maheśvara Viśārada, a scholar of Nadia; Vidyānagara is near Koladvīpa (Kuliyā). The Lord told him personally to worship the Gaṅgā, and stayed with him at Vidyānagara (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 6.18, 15.133–136, 16.207; Ādi 10.85). By tradition he later taught Vedānta to Jīva Gosvāmī in Kāśī (Madhusūdana Vācaspati).

name: Śrī Madhvācārya
add: Nandgram Dham: the third avatāra of Vāyu, after Hanumān and Bhīma (Sumadhva-vijaya). Born traditionally in 1238 (some sources 1199); disappeared traditionally in 1317 at Uḍupī (some sources 1278). Dvaita (Tattvavāda): the eternal five-fold difference between God, souls and matter. Chief works: Brahma-sūtra-bhāṣya, Gītā-bhāṣya, Bhāgavata-tātparya-nirṇaya and about thirty more, together the Sarvamūla.

name: Maheśa Paṇḍita
add: Nandgram Dham: the seventh of the twelve gopālas; with Nityānanda at the festivals of Pāṇihāṭi and Saptagrāma. His śrīpāṭa, founded at Maśipura near Jirāṭ, moved to Beleḍāṅgā near Sukhasāgara and in 1927 to Pālapāḍā near Cākdaha. By one account the youngest of three brothers, with Jagadīśa Paṇḍita and Hiraṇya; Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura calls the evidence inconclusive.

name: Mīnaketana Ramdasa
add: Nandgram Dham: named 75th among Nityānanda's associates (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.53). The chief episode recorded is an all-night saṅkīrtana at Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja's home (Ādi 5).

name: Mukunda Datta
add: Nandgram Dham: native place Cāṅhārā (Cakraśālā by one later account), Paṭiyā, Chittagong. He introduced Gadādhara Paṇḍita to Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi. He left this world on Jyaiṣṭha Pūrṇimā, the day of the Snāna-yātrā (year not recorded).

name: Murāri Gupta Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: his family moved from Śrīhaṭṭa (Sylhet) to Navadvīpa when he was young; the Lord is said to have written the name «Rāmadāsa» on his forehead. His Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Caitanya-caritāmṛta, the «Kaḍacā», is the earliest known life of Śrī Caitanya. His śrīpāṭa and samādhi are near Ballāla Dīghi, east of the Yogapīṭha, Māyāpura.

name: Murāri Māhiti
add: Nandgram Dham: the title Māhiti marks an Oḍiyā temple-service family; his elder brother Śikhi Māhiti was an official of the Jagannātha temple. Sārvabhauma introduced him to the Lord at Kāśī Miśra's house, after the Lord's return from South India (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 10.44); among the Purī devotees who «constantly associated» with the Lord (Ādi 10.136). His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Nandana Ācārya
add: Nandgram Dham: the seventeenth branch of the Caitanya tree (Ādi 10.39). Another tradition gives his father as Caturbhuja and his brothers as Viṣṇudāsa and Gaṅgādāsa (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.43; Caitanya-bhāgavata 3.5.74). In Purī he was named among the Lord's devotees to Pratāparudra and served at the cleaning of the Guṇḍicā and Nṛsiṁha temples and at the Ratha-yātrā. His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Nārada Muni
add: Nandgram Dham: the second ācārya of the Brahma-sampradāya, a mind-born son of Brahmā; in a previous life he served wandering Vaiṣṇava sannyāsīs. His vīṇā was given by Lord Kṛṣṇa (Liṅga Purāṇa). He told Vyāsadeva to write the Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavatam 1.5); his disciples include Dhruva, Prahlāda, Vyāsadeva and Vālmīki. The Nārada-bhakti-sūtra is attributed to him.

name: Śrī Narahari Cakravartī (Ghanaśyāma dāsa)
add: Nandgram Dham: his dīkṣā guru Nṛsiṁha (Narasiṁha) Cakravartī was in the line of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya. Works: Bhakti-ratnākara, Narottama-vilāsa, Śrīnivāsa-carita, Gaura-caritra-samudra, Nāmāmṛta-samudra, Saṅgīta-sāra-saṅgraha, Navadvīpa-dhāma-parikramā. He cooked for and served Rādhā-Govindajī into his seventies.

name: Śrī Narahari Sarakāra Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: Madhumatī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 177). Works: Śrī Kṛṣṇa-bhajanāmṛta, Bhakti-candrikā-paṭala, Śrī Caitanya-sahasranāma and shorter poems. His chief disciple was Locana dāsa Ṭhākura, author of the Caitanya-maṅgala. The year of his disappearance is disputed.
